linkedin.text:
About 1,500 complaints say Block froze or shut Square accounts without notice. That's the FTC's count, and the agency is now in federal court to get Block's records on them.

The FTC's filing says those complaints "allege that Block has wrongfully withheld at least $2.5 million of Square users' payment proceeds since 2022."

Where it stands: the FTC is investigating and hasn't charged Block. It asked a federal court in California on Oct. 7 to make Block answer. Block disputes the claims and agreed to send its answers by Nov. 13 and more by Nov. 30.

A held payout lands on a Friday, when payroll, rent and the produce order are due. That's why I'd check three things this week, whatever you use to take cards:

1. The hold section of your processor agreement: when they can hold your money, for how long, and how they have to tell you.
2. A second way to take payments, set up and tested before you need it.
3. If a hold starts: put it in writing, save every email, and file a complaint with the FTC if it drags on.

Full disclosure: I started SVPay, which is another way for shops to get paid, so weigh my take with that in mind.

Has a processor ever held your payouts, and for how long?

#SmallBusiness

facts.text: The records demand (civil investigative demand) was issued Jan. 22 and holds 47 questions, 21 document requests and four data requests
Block disputes and does not admit the allegations; under a joint filing it answers the 47 questions by Nov. 13 and sends more by Nov. 30

FTC v. Block, Inc., No. 4:26-mc-80299, U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California: a petition to enforce a civil investigative demand, filed Oct 7, 2026; no closing entry. An FTC investigation; no charges filed and no finding against Block.
The petition was filed in the Northern District of California (Oakland), case No. 26-mc-80299 (Bloomberg, via Quartz)
